quarterly_data.signal: WFE VIEW RAISED: asked about the mid-teens 2026 WFE framework the moderator attributed to Nova from May, CFO Guy Kizner said the numbers have moved up - external estimates have been revised up every two months, driven by AI, and on Nova's read of WFE 'it will be above 20%', though he would not name a number (Nova does not forecast WFE internally and refers to market consensus). He noted the market range is still unusually wide four months from year end: 'Gartner talking about 20% growth, TechInsights in the high 20s', with other analysts at 30, 35, 38 - even with the big players' backlog and shipment plans already visible.
quarterly_data.figure: it will be above 20%; Gartner talking about 20% growth, TechInsights in the high 20s

quarterly_data.signal: WHY NOVA IS NOT OUTPERFORMING WFE AS USUAL IN 2026 (the '2x WFE' framing was the moderator's, not management's): Kizner said Nova historically outperforms WFE significantly ('2024, we grew by 30%', '2025, we grew by 31%' while WFE did not grow much) but 2026 breaks the pattern because of investment MIX. Three reasons: (1) NAND contributes to WFE but nothing to Nova because the spend is upgrades, not greenfield capacity; (2) heavy DRAM investment, where metrology intensity is lower than logic; (3) most important, the AI customers did NOT transition to Gate-All-Around - they are 'still using the N-1, 3 nm and 5 nm' and are spending on 3 nm capacity expansions in both the U.S. and Taiwan, so the metrology intensity of 2026 spending went down on mix.
quarterly_data.figure: 2024, we grew by 30%; 2025, we grew by 31%; still using the N-1, 3 nm and 5 nm

quarterly_data.signal: 2027 SETUP BY END MARKET: Kizner expects the mix to swing back in Nova's favour in 2027 - NAND capacity additions would be 'coming from zero to business' for Nova since it is positioned with all the key NAND customers (he called this the longest NAND down cycle, with upgrades-only spend that Nova does not benefit from, and hopes for greenfield in 2027); DRAM stays a significant driver on capacity expansion but with NO metrology-intensity increase until the industry moves to 4F², which he placed in '2028 and going forward'; and logic mix shifts 'much more towards the 2 nm and the Gate-All-Around, and less on the 3 nm', pushing metrology intensity up.
quarterly_data.figure: it will happen in 2028 and going forward

quarterly_data.signal: CAPACITY BUILD BEYOND THE US CLEAN ROOM: Kizner said Nova is 'doubling our production floor'; besides the US expansion it has opened 'a new clean room in Germany' and will open 'a new clean room by the end of this year for the first time in Asia', with CapEx staying focused on infrastructure into 2027 and beyond. He stressed the constraint is not only Nova's own clean-room space but the whole stretched supply chain: Nova gives its vendors forward visibility so they can ramp, and qualifies a second vendor where it identifies a bottleneck, because one crucial vendor can stop Nova meeting demand regardless of floor space.
quarterly_data.figure: doubling our production floor; a new clean room in Germany; a new clean room by the end of this year for the first time in Asia

quarterly_data.signal: HYBRID BONDING IS THE PACKAGING SHARE PRIZE - TIMING GIVEN: Kizner said the main advanced-packaging share-gain opportunity ahead is hybrid bonding, which brings front-end capability into the back end: copper-to-copper bonding requires wafer-to-wafer and die warpage control, CMP uniformity and flatness control, all of which raise metrology intensity and pull in both Nova's dimensional and materials metrology portfolios. The work right now is QUALIFICATIONS - high-volume manufacturing 'capacity is not big story in 2027', it comes later. He added that Nova's materials metrology is not yet exposed to advanced packaging at all and that early customer discussions to apply it there are another growth engine on top of the ancosys and Sentronics acquisitions and the PRISM front-end tools already deployed into packaging.
quarterly_data.figure: the capacity is not big story in 2027

quarterly_data.signal: CHINA GUIDANCE REVISED UP: Kizner said China is 'around 30% of our revenues' today and 25% to 30% of overall WFE spending, and that although Nova said at the start of the year China would be slightly down to flat, the visibility it now has means 'it will be another growth year for China for us on a nominal basis' (still declining as a percentage because other regions grow faster). He treats domestic Chinese metrology vendors as a real risk rather than dismissing them - they have the talent, funds and government support, there is still a capability gap today, and Nova's answer is to keep spending a significant portion of revenue on R&D to keep the gap open.
quarterly_data.figure: it is around 30% of our revenues; 25% to 30% over all WFE spending; it will be another growth year for China for us on a nominal basis
